append.text: Ps 91:8 *Cum exórti fúerint peccatóres sicut fænum* → *Quando os pecadores brotarem como a erva* — the grass springs up, so *erva* by the row's split; no reader remarked (the ambiguity reader heard grass / weeds).

**Ps 91:12 *Et despéxit óculus meus inimícos meos* → *E o meu olho olhou de cima os meus inimigos*** — the same Latin as 53:9, so the same words (rule 6); the Latinist passed it twice. **The v1 stylist named it the worst line of Ps 91 for the *olho olhou* jingle** (proposing *viu do alto*, option). Second psalm with the jingle: **for Gustavo** — if lifted, 53:9 and 91:12 change together.
Ps 91:11 *Et exaltábitur sicut unicórnis cornu meum* → *E será exaltado o meu chifre como o do unicórnio*; the ambiguity reader heard the cuckold's horn again; kept.
Ps 91:11 → *como o do unicórnio* (the genitive reading, = μονοκέρωτος; *unicórnis* can be either case); the ambiguity reader heard the mythical animal — the Latin's.
Ps 91:14 → *nos átrios da casa do nosso Deus* (= 133:1b); unknown to the ambiguity reader again.
Ps 91:12 *in insurgéntibus in me malignántibus* → *dos malvados que se levantam contra mim* — applied.
Ps 91:12 → *malvados* (one of the plural places this row named); no reader remarked.
Ps 91:4 *cum cántico, in cíthara* → *com o cântico, com a cítara* — the colon closes on *cítara* as the Latin on *cíthara* (as 56:9); unknown to the ambiguity reader again.

**Ps 91:4 *In decachórdo, psaltério* (two nouns in the DO Latin; L&S *decachórdum* 'an instrument of ten strings', citing this verse) → *Com o instrumento de dez cordas, com o saltério*** (DRB). v1 *Com as dez cordas* was heard as strings by the Latinist (minor) and the ambiguity reader. 143:9 *in psaltério decachórdo* (the adjective) should take 32:2's *com o saltério de dez cordas*. The ambiguity reader heard *saltério* as the book again.
Ps 91:7 *Vir insípiens … et stultus* → *O homem insensato … e o tolo* — applied.
Ps 91:7 *Vir insípiens* → *O homem insensato* — applied beside *tolo*.
Ps 91:6 *nimis profúndæ factæ sunt* (σφόδρα) → *Muito profundos se tornaram* — as 47:2; no reader remarked.

Ps 91:9 *Ut intéreant in sǽculum sǽculi* (ἐξολεθρευθῶσιν) → *Para que se extingam pelos séculos dos séculos* — the row's *extinguir-se*, kept apart from 91:10 *períbunt → perecerão*; the v1 Latinist (minor) asked *pereçam*, refused for that reason, option.

Ps 91:5 the causative *delectásti me … in factúra tua* (εὔφρανας) → *me alegrastes … com a vossa feitura*, as 29:2 and 64:8; the v2 Latinist (minor) asked *na vossa feitura* for the parallel with *in opéribus* — held (not the Portuguese build of the causative), option.

Ps 91:13 *sicut cedrus Líbani multiplicábitur* → *como o cedro do Líbano se multiplicará*; 91:15 *multiplicabúntur* → *se multiplicarão* — one verb as the Latin (DRB 'grow up' is the option); the ambiguity reader heard 'grow' first.
Ps 91:7 *Vir insípiens non cognóscet* (no object of its own) → *não saberá*, as 13:4; *conhecerá* (MS1932) option; no reader remarked.

**Ps 91:2 *et psállere nómini tuo, Altíssime* → *e entoar salmos, ó Altíssimo, ao vosso nome*** — the vocative moved inside the colon (not to its head as 9:3, because the Responsory splits *Et psállere* off); v2 adds *ó*: the ambiguity reader heard the bare *Altíssimo* as the one sung to. 91:9 *tu autem Altíssimus* → *vós sois o Altíssimo* (the name, echoing 91:2).

terms: | decachórdum | o instrumento de dez cordas | open | Ps 91:4 (a noun in the DO Latin, beside *psaltério*; L&S cites this verse). *decacórdio* (the Latinist's fix) is a dictionary word — refused; *as dez cordas* (v1) heard as strings. 143:9 has the adjective *decachórdo* with *psaltério* → *o saltério de dez cordas* (32:2). |

| factúra | feitura (*me alegrastes, Senhor, com a vossa feitura*) | open | Ps 91:5 only (grep before copying); ποίημα, kept apart from *ópera → obras* in the same verse. v1 *com o que fizestes* (the D16 device) was refused by the Latinist (a noun) and the stylist (vague, a chime); the stylist's *obra* merges the two words — option. |

| úber (adj.) | fecundo (*em misericórdia fecunda … em velhice fecunda*) | open | Ps 91:11, 91:15 (L&S 'rich, fruitful, fertile'; πίων). One word for both places; *abundante* fits mercy, not old age. *fecunda* unknown to the ambiguity reader. 91:11 *misericórdia* is the Latin's against the Greek's ἐλαίῳ (followed). |

| *bene patiéntes erunt* | *passarão bem* | open | Ps 91:15 (a calque of εὐπαθοῦντες). v1 *estarão bem* was flat to the stylist and the ambiguity reader; *passarão bem* the Latinist's (a verb of faring, as pati). *serão bem tratados* (DRB, the stylist) refused — it supplies an agent; *estarão cheios de vigor* (MS1932) option. Watch: *passarão* can be heard as 'pass by'. |
| palma | palmeira (*O justo, como a palmeira, florescerá*) | open | Ps 91:13 (φοῖνιξ); *palma* is the hand or the branch in Brazil. |
| exóriri (plants) | brotar (*Quando os pecadores brotarem como a erva*) | open | Ps 91:8 (ἀνατεῖλαι); MS1932. *surgir* option. |
formulas: | *Bonum est confitéri Dómino: et psállere nómini tuo, Altíssime* (91:2; Offertory / Gradual — missa Quadp1-0, Pent15-0 and others; Responsory *R. Bonum est confitéri Dómino, allelúja: * Et psállere, allelúja* — grep) · *Ad annuntiándum mane misericórdiam tuam, et veritátem tuam per noctem* (91:3; Gradual / Alleluia verse) | *É bom dar graças ao Senhor: * e entoar salmos, ó Altíssimo, ao vosso nome* · *Para anunciar de manhã a vossa misericórdia: * e a vossa verdade durante a noite* | open — Ps 91; each reads alone; the Responsory's *e entoar salmos* stands by itself |

| *Quam magnificáta sunt * ópera tua, Dómine* (91:6a; the Sunday Vespers short responsory and an antiphon, Psalmi major — grep) | *Como se engrandeceram * as vossas obras, Senhor* | open — Ps 91 (*foram engrandecidas*, *são grandes* options) |

| *Justus ut palma florébit: sicut cedrus Líbani multiplicábitur (in domo Dómini)* (91:13–14; versicle *V. Justus ut palma florébit. R. Sicut cedrus Líbani multiplicábitur*; Introit / Gradual of Commune C4a, C5 and Masses of confessors — grep; one form reads *sicut cedrus, quæ in Líbano est*) | *O justo, como a palmeira, florescerá: * como o cedro do Líbano se multiplicará (na casa do Senhor)* | open — Ps 91 (the Latin's order, the stylist's best line; *O justo florescerá como a palmeira* option); each colon reads alone |
